title: When the cache disappears
summary: The layer that absorbs 95% of your reads just went away.

statement.situation: A content site serves 6,000 requests/s, almost all reads. A cache layer normally answers nearly everything, and the database behind it is sized for the leftover trickle. During a routine maintenance window the entire cache layer becomes unavailable for four minutes and then returns empty.
symptoms: The database suddenly receives most of the traffic
Connections fill, latency rises, errors follow, and retries make it worse
When the cache returns it is empty and the database takes another hit
requirements: Keep the site usable during the outage — degrade, don't collapse
The database must survive, and the system must return to normal after the cache comes back
Retries from clients (two, with backoff) must not finish it off
constraints: Database machines have a fixed size
You can't change client retry behaviour

learningObjectives: Why the recovery (cold cache) is its own incident
Capacity for the worst case versus protecting capacity

references.title: AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter

scenarios.name: Cache layer lost for 4 minutes
scenarios.description: 6,000 req/s. The whole cache layer fails at t=60 s and returns empty at t=300 s.

successCriteria.label: At least 80% of requests succeed during the outage
The database is never driven into collapse
Back to ≥ 98% availability within 90 s of the cache returning
